description: A former druidic grove lying fallow and fully reclaimed by nature.

feature.name: Overgrown Battlefield - Passive
feature.question: Why did these groups come to blows? Why is the grove unused now?
feature.text:
There has been a battle here. A PC can make an Instinct Roll to identify evidence of that fight. On a success with Hope, learn all three pieces of information below. On a success with Fear, learn two. On a failure, a PC can mark a Stress to learn one and gain advantage on the next action roll to investigate this environment. A PC with an appropriate background or Experience can learn an additional detail and ask a follow-up question about the scene and get a truthful (if not always complete) answer.

- Traces of a battle (broken weapons and branches, gouges in the ground) litter the ground.
- A moss-covered tree trunk is actually the corpse of a treant.
- Still-standing trees are twisted in strange ways, as if by powerful magic.

Why did these groups come to blows? Why is the grove unused now?

feature.name: Barbed Vines - Action
feature.question: How many vines are there? Where do they grab you? Do they pull you down or lift you off the ground?
feature.text:
Pick a point within the grove. All targets within Very Close range of that point must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take **1d8+3** physical damage and become _Restrained_ by barbed vines. _Restrained_ lasts until they're freed with a successful Finesse or Strength roll or by dealing at least 6 damage to the vines.

How many vines are there? Where do they grab you? Do they pull you down or lift you off the ground?

feature.name: You Are Not Welcome Here - Action
feature.question: What are the grove guardians concealing? What threat to the forest could the PCs confront to appease the Dryad?
feature.text:
A Young Dryad, two Sylvan Soldiers, and a number of Minor Treants equal to the number of PCs appear to confront the party for their intrusion.

What are the grove guardians concealing? What threat to the forest could the PCs confront to appease the Dryad?

feature.name: Defiler - Action
feature.question: What color does the grass turn as the elemental appears? How does the chaos warp insects and small wildlife within the grove?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to summon a Minor Chaos Elemental drawn to the echoes of violence and discord. They appear within Far range of a chosen PC and immediately take the spotlight.

What color does the grass turn as the elemental appears? How does the chaos warp insects and small wildlife within the grove?

impulses: Draw in the curious, echo the past
name: Abandoned Grove
potential_adversaries: Beasts (Bear, Dire Wolf, Glass Snake), Grove Guardians (Minor Treant, Sylvan Soldier, Young Dryad)

description: A twisting warren of disused tunnels carved out of the bedrock by a doomed mining outfit.

feature.name: Pitch Black - Passive
feature.question: What fuel does the party's light source use, and how long will it last? What unwanted attention does the light attract?
feature.text:
There is no light, natural or otherwise, in these underground mining tunnels. Ask the PCs what they use for light or how they otherwise find their way in the dark. PCs without a reliable source of light make action and reaction rolls with disadvantage.

What fuel does the party's light source use, and how long will it last? What unwanted attention does the light attract?

feature.name: Labyrinth - Passive
feature.question: What did miners previously extract here? Who in the party knows how to navigate below ground? What are the PCs most afraid might happen to them down here?
feature.text:
The party must complete a Progress Countdown (4) to find their way through the mines. Each time a PC rolls with Hope while finding their way through, they discover one of the curiosities below.

- An unmined vein of precious metals or gemstones
- Various mining tools, including a broken (but mendable) mine cart made of adamantine
- Psychic echoes of the miners' tragic end
- The desiccated corpses of miners who lost their way in the tunnels
- Tattered remnants of darkweave spider silk

What did miners previously extract here? Who in the party knows how to navigate below ground? What are the PCs most afraid might happen to them down here?

feature.name: Into the Spider's Web - Action
feature.question: How does the Darkweave Queen use her lair to her advantage? What remnants of her past meals can the party find here?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to summon a Darkweave Queen inside her gossamer-strewn lair. She drops from the ceiling within Close range of a PC and immediately takes the spotlight.

How does the Darkweave Queen use her lair to her advantage? What remnants of her past meals can the party find here?

feature.name: Impending Collapse - Reaction
feature.question: What other signs of instability does the mine offer the party? What new dangers does the tunnel system's new configuration expose the party to?
feature.text:
_Countdown (2)._ The first time the PCs roll with Fear, describe how the ground subtly vibrates as rocks shift overhead and activate the countdown. It ticks down when a PC rolls with Fear. When it triggers, each PC must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take **1d8+3** physical damage and become temporarily _Restrained_ by the rubble.

What other signs of instability does the mine offer the party? What new dangers does the tunnel system's new configuration expose the party to?

impulses: Poison the party with deadly gasses, rumble and collapse, split the party, turn them around
name: Abandoned Mine
potential_adversaries: Darkweave Spiders (Darkweave *Crawler, Darkweave Spinner, Darkweave Swarmlings*), Miner Ghosts (*Poltergeist, Will-o'-the-Wisps*)

The Difficulty of this environment equals that of the adversary with the highest Difficulty.

When a PC starts the ambush on unsuspecting adversaries, you lose 2 Fear and the first attack roll a PC makes has advantage.

description: A lightning-powered laboratory built by a scientist searching for the secret to immortality.

feature.name: Cabinet of Curiosities - Passive
feature.question: What was the alchemist studying? What smell overwhelms you as you shuffle through their things?
feature.text:
The workshop's shelves, cupboards, and tables are cluttered with macabre bric-a-brac, including body parts in jars of formaldehyde and bloody surgical implements. Once per scene, a PC can make an Instinct Roll to look for something useful in the chaos.

What was the alchemist studying? What smell overwhelms you as you shuffle through their things?

feature.name: Strange Machinery - Passive
feature.question: What do these machines do? What do these instruments measure?
feature.text:
The workshop contains numerous pieces of bizarre technology and scientific instrumentation. A PC can make a Knowledge Roll to try to figure out how it works. On a success, they can get it running. On a failure, they break something and take **1d8+4** direct magic damage as they're shocked by electricity and doused in caustic chemicals.

What do these machines do? What do these instruments measure?

feature.name: It's Alive! - Action
feature.question: What was the alchemist trying to achieve with this experiment? Where did they get the materials for it?
feature.text:
_Consequence Countdown (6)_. A thunderstorm gathers overhead, threatening to jolt the lightning rod assembly installed atop the workshop. Activate the countdown and narrate how the storm's power increases each time it ticks down when a PC makes an action roll. When it triggers, lightning strikes the rod assembly and overloads the workshop machinery, which explodes after resurrecting one of the alchemist's abandoned projects. Each target within Close range of the machinery must succeed on an Agility Reaction Roll or take **1d10** magic damage. Summon a Failed Experiment at a location within the workshop and gain a Fear for each PC within Very Close range of it.

What was the alchemist trying to achieve with this experiment? Where did they get the materials for it?

impulses: Break down the barrier between life and death, draw down lightning from the heavens, overclock the machinery
name: Alchemist’s Abandoned Workshop
potential_adversaries: Lab Leftovers (Construct, Minor Fire Elemental, Patchwork Zombie Hulk, Swarm of Rats)

description: The economic heart of the settlement, with local artisans, traveling merchants, and patrons across social classes.

feature.name: Tip the Scales - Passive
feature.question: Will any coin be accepted, or only local currency? How overt are the PCs in offering this bribe?
feature.text:
PCs can gain advantage on a Presence Roll by offering a handful of gold as part of the interaction.

Will any coin be accepted, or only local currency? How overt are the PCs in offering this bribe?

feature.name: Unexpected Find - Action
feature.question: What cost beyond gold will the merchant ask for in exchange for this rarity?
feature.text:
Reveal to the PCs that one of the merchants has something they want or need, such as food from their home, a rare book, magical components, a dubious treasure map, or a magical key.

What cost beyond gold will the merchant ask for in exchange for this rarity?

feature.name: Sticky Fingers - Action
feature.question: What drove this person to pickpocketing? Where is the thief's hideout and how has it avoided notice?
feature.text:
A thief tries to steal something from a PC. The PC must succeed on an Instinct Roll to notice the thief or lose an item of the GM's choice as the thief escapes to a Close distance. To retrieve the stolen item, the PCs must complete a Progress Countdown (6) to chase down the thief before the thief completes a Consequence Countdown (4) and escapes to their hideout.

What drove this person to pickpocketing? Where is the thief's hideout and how has it avoided notice?

feature.name: Crowd Closes In - Reaction
feature.question: Where does the crowd's movement carry them? How do they feel about being alone but surrounded?
feature.text:
When one of the PCs splits from the group, the crowds shift and cut them off  from the party.

Where does the crowd's movement carry them? How do they feel about being alone but surrounded?

impulses: Buy low, and sell high, tempt and tantalize with wares from near and far
name: Bustling Marketplace
potential_adversaries: Guards (Bladed Guard, Head Guard), Masked Thief, Merchant

description: A wretched stretch of slimy water, toxic creatures, and decay.

feature.name: Swamp Sickness - Passive
feature.question: Is the swamp teeming with life, filled with decay, or both? What force blighted this swamp, and what signs of its origins remain?
feature.text:
At the end of a long rest, each PC must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or gain a d4 Sickened Die, starting with the 1 value facing up. If a PC fails this roll and already has a Sickened Die, they increase the value by 1, to a maximum value of 4. A PC with a Sickened Die gains a penalty to their action rolls equal to its value. When a PC with a Sickened Die would clear a HP, they can decrease the value of their Sickened Die by 1 instead. When the die's value would fall to 0, remove it.

Is the swamp teeming with life, filled with decay, or both? What force blighted this swamp, and what signs of its origins remain?

feature.name: Soggy and Slogging It - Passive
feature.question: What creatures, living or otherwise, lurk beneath the water's murky surface? Where or how do the PCs find relief from the stinking water?
feature.text:
When a PC moves as part of an action, they can only move up to Very Close range. Action rolls made to move farther than Very Close range have disadvantage. Before rolling, a PC can mark a Stress to remove this disadvantage.

What creatures, living or otherwise, lurk beneath the water's murky surface? Where or how do the PCs find relief from the stinking water?

feature.name: Rotbloom - Action
feature.question: How can you tell the plants that emit this pollen are carnivorous? What nightmares or dreamscapes does the pollen's scent conjure?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to dust an area within Far range in noxious pollen. Each target in that area must succeed on a Strength or Instinct Reaction Roll or take **1d6+3** magic damage and become _Vulnerable_ until the end of the scene.

How can you tell the plants that emit this pollen are carnivorous? What nightmares or dreamscapes does the pollen's scent conjure?

feature.name: Dancing Lights - Action
feature.question: What does the lost PC see in the lights that draws them into the darkness? What other glimpses of surprising beauty do the PCs encounter here?
feature.text:
At the start of a rest, you can **spend a Fear** to have floating orbs enthrall the weary and lure a PC deeper into the swamp. A different PC can use a downtime move to make an action roll to search for them. On a success, both PCs return to camp and can choose downtime moves as normal. On a failure—or if no one searches for them—the lost PC returns hours later, covered in mud and worse, and can't choose downtime moves until their next rest.

What does the lost PC see in the lights that draws them into the darkness? What other glimpses of surprising beauty do the PCs encounter here?

impulses: Corrupt, emphasize putrescence, reveal the twisted and unnatural, sicken
name: Corrupted Swamp
potential_adversaries: Any Undead (Skeleton, Zombie, Spectral Guardian), Giant Rat, Green Ooze, Tangle Bramble

description: A steep, rocky cliffside tall enough to make traversal dangerous.

feature.name: The Climb - Passive
feature.question: What strange formations are the stones arranged in? What ominous warnings did previous adventurers leave?
feature.text:
Climbing up the cliffside uses a Progress Countdown (12). It ticks down according to the following criteria when the PCs make an action roll to climb:

- **Critical Success:** Tick down 3
- **Success with Hope:** Tick down 2
- **Success with Fear:** Tick down 1
- **Failure with Hope:** No advancement
- **Failure with Fear:** Tick up 1 When the countdown triggers, the party has made it to the top of the cliff.

What strange formations are the stones arranged in? What ominous warnings did previous adventurers leave?

feature.name: Pitons Left Behind - Passive
feature.question: What do the shape and material of these pitons tell you about the previous climbers? How far apart are they from one another?
feature.text:
Previous climbers left behind large metal rods that climbers can use to aid their ascent. If a PC using the pitons fails an action roll to climb, they can mark a Stress instead of ticking the countdown up.

What do the shape and material of these pitons tell you about the previous climbers? How far apart are they from one another?

feature.name: Fall - Action
feature.question: How can you tell many others have fallen here before? What lives in these walls that might try to scare adventurers into falling for an easy meal?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to have a PC's handhold fail, plummeting them toward the ground. If they aren't saved on the next action, they hit the ground and tick up the countdown by 2. The PC takes **1d12** physical damage if the countdown is between 8 and 12, **2d12** between 4 and 7, and **3d12** at 3 or lower.

How can you tell many others have fallen here before? What lives in these walls that might try to scare adventurers into falling for an easy meal?

impulses: Cast the unready down to a rocky doom, draw people in with promise of what lies at the top
name: Cliffside Ascent
potential_adversaries: Construct, Deeproot Defender, Giant Scorpion, Glass Snake

description: A sprawling cemetery filled with crumbling headstones, twisted trees possessed by the dead, and crypts overgrown with moss and ivy.

feature.name: Room for One More - Passive
feature.question: What new information or experience does a PC gain from becoming a specter? How can the party reunite the PC's spirit with their flesh? What happens if their ritual goes wrong?
feature.text:
If a PC marks their last HP while in the graveyard, they become a _Specter_ instead of making a death move. While a _Specter_, a PC can communicate with the living but can't interact with the physical world, and they must stay within Close range of their corpse or cross through the veil of death. This condition is cleared when the PC clears a HP.

What new information or experience does a PC gain from becoming a specter? How can the party reunite the PC's spirit with their flesh? What happens if their ritual goes wrong?

feature.name: Hallowed Ground - Passive
feature.question: Who sanctified this place, and what happened to them? What holy relics can be found here?
feature.text:
At the center of the graveyard is a seemingly undisturbed chapel. On a successful Instinct Roll, a PC can discover this structure is sanctified against the cemetery's denizens. While inside the chapel, the PCs have advantage on action rolls to fight or drive off  spirits and undead.

Who sanctified this place, and what happened to them? What holy relics can be found here?

feature.name: Misty Miasma - Action
feature.question: What horrors do the PCs see in the fog? What disorienting smell does the miasma emit?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to fill an area within Far range with a low-lying ectoplasmic fog that seeps up through the soggy earth. When a PC rolls with Fear while in the miasma, they must mark a Stress.

What horrors do the PCs see in the fog? What disorienting smell does the miasma emit?

feature.name: The Dead Arise - Action
feature.question: Who were these people in life? Why were they buried here? Why won't they stay dead?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to have undead hands burst forth from the ground beneath a PC. The target must succeed on an Agility or Presence Reaction Roll or mark a Stress and become temporarily _Restrained_ as hands grasp them.

Who were these people in life? Why were they buried here? Why won't they stay dead?

feature.name: The Dead Don't Die Easy - Reaction
feature.question: Who commanded this land to reject death? How do the dead come back different here?
feature.text:
When an adversary would mark their last HP, roll a **d6**. On a result of 5 or 6, the adversary doesn't mark it.

Who commanded this land to reject death? How do the dead come back different here?

impulses: Bury them six feet deep, choke with fog, lure with promises of entombed treasure, unleash the restless dead
name: Cursed Graveyard
potential_adversaries: Corrupted Spirits (Deeproot Defender, *Phantom*), Living Dead (Skeleton Warrior, Zombie Pack, Patchwork Zombie Hulk)

description: A community-wide celebration featuring way too much drink, food, and fun.

feature.name: Loose Lips & Fast Friends - Passive
feature.question: What is everyone celebrating? Where's the party? Who's footing the bill?
feature.text:
Everyone is here to have a good time. PCs have advantage on Presence Rolls to socialize with other revelers.

What is everyone celebrating? Where's the party? Who's footing the bill?

feature.name: The Evening's Entertainment - Action
feature.question: What does the host want to see or hear more than anything else? What can they offer the PCs in return?
feature.text:
The host of the feast kicks off  the entertainment portion of the evening. Each PC can make an action roll to initiate a performance, competition, or other lighthearted diversion. A PC who succeeds becomes an _Honored_ _Guest_. Until the feast ends, an _Honored Guest_ can claim a gift from the host, then clear the condition.

What does the host want to see or hear more than anything else? What can they offer the PCs in return?

feature.name: "There's Always That One…" - Action
feature.question: What makes this dud so unpleasant? What's something the PC cares about that the dud constantly diminishes or dismisses? What boring or awful thing can the dud not shut up about?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to _Trap_ a PC in conversation with the most unpleasant person at the party until the PC succeeds on an action roll to extricate themself from this social black hole. While _Trapped_, a PC can't make action rolls except to try to clear this condition. When a _Trapped_ PC fails an action roll, they must mark a Stress.

What makes this dud so unpleasant? What's something the PC cares about that the dud constantly diminishes or dismisses? What boring or awful thing can the dud not shut up about?

feature.name: Last Call - Reaction
feature.question: What crazy stories do the PCs share with one another as they leave the party? Who do the PCs see unexpectedly canoodling afterward?
feature.text:
After a long night, the partygoers start filtering out. When the feast concludes, all PCs who participated in the festivities clear all Stress and gain a Hope. Additionally, each _Honored Guest_ clears all HP and gains an additional Hope, then clears the condition. Each PC who overindulged must succeed on a Strength Reaction Roll or become _Hungover_ until their next rest. While _Hungover_, a PC gains a -1 penalty to action rolls.

What crazy stories do the PCs share with one another as they leave the party? Who do the PCs see unexpectedly canoodling afterward?

impulses: Bring everyone together, celebrate a momentous occasion, encourage revelrous abandon
name: Grand Feast
potential_adversaries: Apprentice Assassin, Guard, Merchant, Petty Noble, Sellsword, Spy

description: The party must fend off  multiple waves of enemies long enough for an ally to complete an important objective.

feature.name: Bodyguards - Passive
feature.question: Who are the PCs protecting, and what is the Charge trying to do? Who wants to stop them? What will happen if the Charge isn't able to complete their task?
feature.text:
The PCs must protect an NPC (their "Charge") long enough for the Charge to complete a task, such as finishing a magical ritual or repairing a mechanical device. At the start of the scene, activate a Task Countdown with a value equal to the number of PCs in the scene. It ticks down when the PCs defeat a wave of adversaries. When it triggers, the Charge completes their task.

Who are the PCs protecting, and what is the Charge trying to do? Who wants to stop them? What will happen if the Charge isn't able to complete their task?

feature.name: "I Must Not Fail!" - Passive
feature.question: Why is this task so important to the Charge? What has the power to break their resolve?
feature.text:
When the first wave of adversaries appears, place a Resolve Countdown next to the Charge with a value equal to the number of PCs in the scene. When an adversary makes an attack against the Charge, the attack automatically succeeds and ticks down the Resolve Countdown. When it triggers, the Charge either flees, dies, or becomes incapacitated.

Why is this task so important to the Charge? What has the power to break their resolve?

feature.name: Swarming Multitudes - Passive
feature.question: Where does these foes' newfound power come from? Is there any way to cut them off from it?
feature.text:
All adversaries gain the "Relentless (2)" feature: They can be spotlighted up to two times per GM turn. Spend Fear as usual to spotlight them.

Where does these foes' newfound power come from? Is there any way to cut them off from it?

feature.name: Waves upon Waves - Reaction
feature.question: Where do these adversaries come from? Who leads them from the shadows?
feature.text:
When there are no adversaries in the scene, summon a wave of adversaries at Far range from the Charge. Each wave comprises two Tier 1 Minions for each PC in the scene.

Where do these adversaries come from? Who leads them from the shadows?

impulses: Crash waves of enemies upon the party's shores, never let them breathe, target their charge

potential_adversaries: Guards, Jagged Knives, Pirates, Skeletons, Zombies

description: Commoners and nobles alike gather from the surrounding area for a weeklong celebration.

feature.name: Remember, Remember - Passive
feature.question: What are the locals celebrating? What is the festival famous for? How did the PCs first hear about it?
feature.text:
This time of year marks an important anniversary or astronomical event, such as the founding of the town or the summer solstice. On a successful Knowledge Roll, a PC can answer one of the questions below (or two, if they critically succeed). On a failure, they answer one question, but you decide which part of their answer is inaccurate and gain a Fear.

- The festival celebrates a crop or export that is critical to the economy here. What is it?
- Why didn't the festival happen last year?
- This festival is similar to another one held in a neighboring region. What makes them different?

What are the locals celebrating? What is the festival famous for? How did the PCs first hear about it?

feature.name: Political Machinations - Passive
feature.question: What new crisis is on everyone's lips? Why can't this community solve the problem on its own? What reward can they offer the PCs in exchange for their aid?
feature.text:

A PC can stick their nose in the goings-on by making a Presence Roll. On a success, they make a connection to a local luminary who can give them a job, share important information, or make useful introductions. On a failure, they must mark a Stress.

What new crisis is on everyone's lips? Why can't this community solve the problem on its own? What reward can they offer the PCs in exchange for their aid?

feature.name: "Let the Games Begin!" - Action
feature.question: What skills or abilities does this competition test? What does the victor win? Why is failure not an option for the PCs or their rivals?
feature.text:
One of the festival's signature events is a sporting competition or series of games. If one or more PCs throw their hat into the ring, introduce rival competitors for them to face off  against. To claim victory, the PCs must complete a Progress Countdown (5) to win events or score points before their rivals complete a Consequence Countdown (5).

What skills or abilities does this competition test? What does the victor win? Why is failure not an option for the PCs or their rivals?

feature.name: Legendary Local - Action
feature.question: Is this a singular entity or a mantle passed from person to person? What distinctive form do they possess? What is the source of their power to grant boons and banes?
feature.text:
The festival culminates in the arrival of a figure from local folklore who performs special duties for the local community, such as giving treats to children, heckling the gentry, or blessing next year's crops. If the PCs show this figure the proper deference and respect, they gain an appropriate blessing, such as a cryptic prophecy or a magical trinket, and gain **1d4** Hope to distribute among the party. If they insult the figure, they take **1d6+2** magic damage as the figure curses them, and you gain a Fear.

Is this a singular entity or a mantle passed from person to person? What distinctive form do they possess? What is the source of their power to grant boons and banes?

impulses: Express local culture and history, forge new relationships, reinforce community
name: Local Festival
potential_adversaries: Festival Security (Bladed Guard, Head Guard), Local Luminaries (Commoner, Merchant, Petty Noble), Sundry Ne'er-Do-Wells (Jagged Knife Bandit, Lackey)

- A promising job for the party involving a nearby threat or situation
- Local folklore that relates to something they've seen

Who has what kind of information? What gossip do the locals start spreading about the PCs?

feature.name: Sing For Your Supper - Passive

What piece do you perform? What does that piece mean to you? When's the last time you performed it for a crowd?

feature.name: Mysterious Stranger - Action

What do they want? What's their impression of the PCs? What mannerisms or accessories do they have?

feature.name: Someone Comes to Town - Action
feature.question: Did they know the PCs were here? What do they want in this town?

Did they know the PCs were here? What do they want in this town?

feature.name: Bar Fight! - Action
feature.question: Who started the fight? What will it take to stop it?
feature.text:
**Spend a Fear** to have a bar fight erupt in the tavern. When a PC tries to move through the tavern while the fight persists, they must succeed on an Agility or Presence Roll or take **1d6+2** physical damage from a wild swing or thrown object. Who started the fight? What will it take to stop it?

description: A small town on the outskirts of a nation or region, close to a dungeon, tombs, or other adventuring destinations.

feature.name: Rumors Abound - Passive
feature.question: What news do the PCs have that they could pass along to curious travelers? What do the locals think about these events?
feature.text:

feature.name: The Summoning - Reaction

feature.text:
_Countdown (6)._ When the party enters the dungeon, activate the countdown. It ticks down when a PC succeeds on an action roll to navigate the passages. When it triggers, the PCs reach the deepest, darkest, best-defended part of the dungeon.

What reward lies at the heart of the maze? Who built this labyrinth to protect it?

feature.name: Deep Pockets - Passive

How did these creatures come to be here? What were they doing when the PCs encountered them?

What kinds of traps and hazards fill this dungeon? What does their construction tell you about whoever designed them? Have any of them been triggered prior to the party's arrival?

feature.name: Divine Censure - Reaction

feature.name: Unmaking - Action

feature.name: Outer Realms Predators - Action

feature.name: Into the Multiverse - Passive

Where (or when) does the party want to go? Where is that portal located, and who controls that area?

Who has the item the party needs? What do they want in return?

feature.name: Don't Make Waves - Passive
feature.question: What has the party done (or what do they plan to do) that draws the attention and ire of the city officials? How can they fix the problem they caused?
feature.text:

feature.name: An Offer You Can't Refuse - Action

Which faction offers the party their support? Who do they want the party to act against?

description: The mysterious, luminous, and isolated ruins of a long-lost lunar kingdom that echoes with forgotten magic and ancient technology.

feature.question: Which PCs are put on trial? What are they accused of? What potential penalties would a guilty verdict bring?
feature.text:
At the end of the proceedings, a jury votes whether to acquit or convict the party. When the court is called to order, have the prosecution present its case against the PCs and start a Countdown (9). It ticks down when a PC makes an action roll. When it triggers, the PCs and GM roll their Judgment Dice. If the party's total result meets or exceeds the GM's, the jury acquits them.

Which PCs are put on trial? What are they accused of? What potential penalties would a guilty verdict bring?

feature.name: Counsel for the Defense - Passive
feature.question: What is the weakest part of the prosecution's case? What is the strongest part of the party's defense?
feature.text:
A PC can make an action roll to argue for their innocence (such as a Knowledge Roll to interpret the letter of the law, a Presence Roll to play on the jury's emotions, or an Instinct Roll to point out holes in the prosecution's case). On a success, the party gains a **d6** Judgment Die. On a critical success, they gain two. On a failure, the prosecution rebuts the PC's argument, and you gain a **d6** Judgment Die.

What is the weakest part of the prosecution's case? What is the strongest part of the party's defense?

feature.name: Counsel for the Prosecution - Action
feature.question: Who leads the prosecution, and what is their relationship to the Time Council? What magic or technology does this court rely on to present and record evidence?
feature.text:
The prosecution introduces a damning piece of evidence (such as an eyewitness testimony, test results, or a physical exhibit taken from the scene of the crime), and you gain a **d6** Judgment Die. A PC can mark a Stress to attempt a rebuttal of the evidence with a Knowledge, Instinct, or Presence Reaction Roll. On a success, the party gains the Judgment Die instead of you. On a failure, you gain an additional **d6** Judgment Die.

Who leads the prosecution, and what is their relationship to the Time Council? What magic or technology does this court rely on to present and record evidence?

feature.name: "Order in the Court!" - Reaction
feature.question: Is this court's authority worthy of respect? What besides the might of the Time Council and its enforcers justifies their control over the timeline?
feature.text:
When the PCs attempt to escape or end the trial through force, summon a number of Temporal Enforcers equal to the number of PCs in the scene within Close range and immediately spotlight one.
